summary.headline: Juniper Hotels Q2 FY27 total income rose 10% to INR258 crore and PAT more than doubled to INR37.2 crore, helped by a 50% fall in finance cost.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 8% to INR249.5 crore and total income grew 10% to INR258.1 crore, with EBITDA at INR91.4 crore (about 35% margin versus 37% a year earlier). Below EBITDA, finance cost fell 50% to INR15.3 crore and PAT rose 121% to INR37.2 crore. Management said ARR grew 8.6% to INR11,514 and occupancy held at 75%, with RevPAR up 12%. Westin Bangalore opened its 238-room Phase 1 in October, and a binding MoU was signed to acquire Novotel Imagicaa (287 keys) for about INR248 crore.

segments.name: Andaz Delhi
segments.commentary: Q2 top line INR83 crore vs INR77 crore YoY (+7%); growth was rate-driven with flat occupancy, supported by events in Delhi.

segments.name: Westin Bangalore (new)
segments.commentary: 238-room Phase 1 soft-opened in October 2026; walk-in guests after Diwali and online bookings from 15 December. FY28 revenue guided at INR100-125 crore at 38-40% margin.

segments.name: Novotel Imagicaa (acquisition)
segments.commentary: 287 keys in Khopoli; binding MoU at about INR80 lakh per key (~INR248 crore). Currently generates about INR60-65 crore top line; expected to contribute from Q4 FY27 and about INR75-80 crore in FY28.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of achieving the FY27 budget with double-digit revenue growth, with H2 (about 60% of annual revenue) expected to be stronger.
Corporate-level EBITDA margin target of 42% for FY27, against 42% in FY26 (operating level ~44-45%); Q2 was hit by HLP, GST and travel-agent commission costs.
Westin Bangalore full-quarter revenue in Q4 FY27; Novotel consolidation in Q4 FY27.
Target to double inventory and EBITDA by FY30-31 (multi-year). Post-completion ROCE of about 19% expected.
Company does not intend to breach debt-to-EBITDA of 2.6x; about 25-30% of the roughly INR2,000 crore capex plan to be spent over the next 18 months.
capex_capacity: Westin Bangalore Phase 1 (238 keys) opened October 2026; Phase 2 (275 keys) under construction, operational by FY29; combined 513 keys with combined development investment of about INR850 crore.
Grand Hyatt New Delhi (~550 keys, 700,000 sq ft, 2.5-acre site): concept approved, groundbreaking expected Q4 FY27; negligible upfront land cost, ROCE of 21%, and a 5-year licence fee moratorium.
Grand Hyatt Guwahati (277 keys including branded residences): concept designs done, civil tendering underway, groundbreaking expected Q3 FY27; draft brand term sheets signed.
Kaziranga luxury wildlife resort: completion expected by FY30. Mumbai commercial tower: groundbreaking early FY28.

Five projects carry an outgo of about INR2,000 crore; further brownfield assets of about 400 rooms under discussion, with two advanced-stage deals (one ~300-room built asset needing extensive renovation, one smaller asset) expected next financial year.
demand_pricing: Q2 ARR rose 8.6% to INR11,514 with occupancy at 75%; management cited 9% ARR growth and 12% RevPAR growth for the portfolio.
Corporate travel and F&B supported Mumbai, Delhi and Ahmedabad; management expects social and MICE demand to lift H2.
Mumbai rates reportedly INR13,500-14,000; management sees Grand Hyatt Mumbai unaffected by Terminal 1 moving to Navi Mumbai.
Westin Bangalore starting ARR not expected below INR13,500-14,000; F&B expected at 30-35% of revenue in Phase 1, rising to about 40% at full 513 keys.
Bangalore comp set cited: Taj Bangalore (370 keys), Leela Bhartiya City (281 keys), plus new Hyatt Centric and Moxy.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Andaz growing only 10% when peers in Delhi report about 20%, and what drove the rise in other expenses (INR81 crore to ~INR97 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Andaz revenue was INR83 crore vs INR77 crore (+7%), rate-driven with flat occupancy. The cost rise was mainly HLP (gas prices, Middle East conflict, ~INR1.5-2 crore) and ~INR2 crore of GST 2.0 ITC loss on rooms sold below INR7,500. Gas equipment is being replaced with electric.

qa_highlights.question: What are the timelines and stabilised numbers for Westin Bangalore and the brownfield pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Online bookings open 15 December; Q4 FY27 gets a full quarter. FY28 revenue guided at INR100-125 crore at 38-40% margin. About 400 further rooms are in discussion; the two other advanced deals are expected to surface in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is Novotel Imagicaa's revenue outlook and how will the theme-park tie-up work?
qa_highlights.answer: Current top line is INR60-65 crore, targeted at about INR80 crore in year one post-consolidation. No discounted rates are committed; the hotel will price at market and partner with the park in off-season. Full repositioning to upper upscale later, with ARR up ~35% and top line more than doubling.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin outlook and the cost bridge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 42% corporate EBITDA margin target for FY27 (FY26 was 42% corporate, 44-45% operating). Q2 was impacted by HLP, GST, travel-agent commission and one-time costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and peak debt plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of about INR2,000 crore, with about 25% (within 25-30%) to be spent over the next 18 months. Company intends not to exceed 2.6x debt-to-EBITDA; net debt currently 1.4x.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the ROFO assets (Hyatt Regency Mumbai, Chennai) and promoter asset merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give specifics. Any promoter assets would come to shareholders for a majority-of-minority decision. Management said the ROFO should not be dwelt upon, and that the company is not saying it is dropped.

risks_watch: Elevated gas and HLP costs (Middle East conflict) and GST 2.0 ITC loss could keep margins under pressure until the gas-to-electric switch is complete.
Execution of about INR2,000 crore capex across five greenfield projects and the Westin Phase 2 / Novotel ramp-up; Novotel's ARR and top-line targets depend on a renovation not yet scheduled.
ROFO-linked promoter assets (Hyatt Regency Mumbai, Chennai) remain unresolved and undisclosed; no timeline was given.
Q3 MPS compliance dilution: mode of fundraise still being evaluated with advisers.
Delhi growth relied on event-driven rate gains; occupancy was flat. Watch Q3/Q4 Delhi performance and Grand Hyatt Mumbai after T1 shift.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating momentum and H2 outlook, but evasive on the ROFO and promoter-asset pipeline and on the Novotel ARR path, and unwilling to give numerical guidance beyond FY27 and the FY28 Bangalore/Novotel ranges.
key_quotes: Our Q2 results show strong resilience of our operating portfolio and build a solid foundation for H2 and the full Financial Year 2027.
Net debt stood at approximately INR633 crores at 1.4 times EBITDA giving headroom for additional debt for strategic acquisitions.
I would let Sandeep give the numbers, but for an asset like this, I would imagine that you would take about in the first phase when we have the 238 rooms about 30% to 35% F&B revenue.

growth.why: Management is confident of achieving the FY27 budget with double-digit revenue growth, backed by Westin Bangalore Phase 1 (238 keys, opened Oct 2026), the Novotel Imagicaa acquisition contributing from Q4 FY27 (INR75-80 crore FY28), and H2 seasonality (about 60% of revenue), though H1 revenue grew only ~10% and Q2 revenue grew 8%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Corporate EBITDA margin target of 42% for FY27 matches FY26, but Q2 margin fell to ~35% from 37% on HLP, GST 2.0 ITC loss and travel-agent commissions, so expansion is conditional on gas-to-electric switch and H2 seasonality.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Westin Bangalore Phase 1 (238 keys) opened Oct 2026, Novotel Imagicaa (287 keys, ~INR248 crore binding MoU) consolidates from Q4 FY27, and Grand Hyatt New Delhi groundbreaking is slated for Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Westin Bangalore full-quarter revenue in Q4 FY27 and Novotel consolidation add room capacity, with occupancy at 75% and RevPAR up 12%, though H1 revenue grew only ~10%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: About INR2,000 crore capex across five projects is already committed, with 25-30% to be spent over 18 months, and utilisation is only 75% so the pipeline is largely under way rather than new.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is only confident of meeting the FY27 budget with double-digit revenue growth, while H1 revenue grew ~10% and Q2 grew only 8%, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 margin fell ~2 points on HLP, GST and commission costs, and Delhi growth was rate-driven with flat occupancy at 75%, so FY27 margin or revenue targets could slip if H2 does not deliver.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Westin Bangalore Phase 1 soft-opened Oct 2026 with online bookings from 15 Dec, and Novotel Imagicaa is targeted at INR75-80 crore revenue in FY28 with a theme-park tie-up.

rows.label: Grand Hyatt Guwahati groundbreaking (277 keys)
rows.why: Concept designs done, civil tendering underway, and groundbreaking expected Q3 FY27 with draft brand term sheets signed.

rows.label: Brownfield pipeline of ~400 rooms
rows.why: About 400 rooms under discussion with two advanced-stage deals (one ~300-room built asset needing renovation) expected to surface next financial year, but no deals are signed.

rows.label: Net debt down to 1.4x EBITDA
rows.why: Gross borrowing fell to INR703 crore from INR739 crore in March 2026, net debt is down ~INR87 crore to INR633 crore, and finance cost halved to INR15.3 crore, so the 2.6x cap is not close to binding.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 seasonality, the Westin Bangalore opening and FY27 double-digit growth, but evasive on the ROFO promoter assets and the Novotel ARR path; analysts pressed on Andaz growth lagging Delhi peers and the rise in other expenses.
